articles.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Arch Manning Or Dante Moore At No. 1 Overall?
articles.summary: Four QBs come off the board in the first round of our mock draft kicking off both the NFL and college football seasons.
articles.body: What better way to celebrate the return of college football and the NFL than with a fresh mock draft? Much will change between now and April 29, 2027, so take this forecast as it is intended — a projection of the current top prospects at the college level coupled with the anticipated needs of NFL teams. As always, it will be fun to monitor how both change over the course of the season. Of course, among the many things that will certainly change in the coming months is the selection order. For the purposes of this mock, we’re taking the inverse order of DraftKings' latest Super Bowl odds. 1. Arizona Cardinals: Arch Manning, QB, Texas With a subpar roster (including at quarterback) and forced to compete against three legitimate Super Bowl contenders within their division, the Cardinals have the easiest route to the No. 1 selection. Manning isn’t without his flaws, but there are plenty of signs that he could be the sort of franchise-changer the Cardinals need to become relevant again. 2. Miami Dolphins: Dante Moore, QB, Oregon I’m more bullish on Malik Willis as a starting quarterback in the NFL than the folks at DraftKings seem to be, but like the aforementioned Cardinals, it seems unlikely that Miami is going to jump in the standings given its own limitations as well as its schedule. I would love to match Willis with Ohio State’s phenomenal receiver Jeremiah Smith here, but the opportunity to land a blue-chip quarterback doesn’t come often, and Moore is certainly that. He is currently a more instinctive and accurate passer than Manning and looks like a lock at this point to be among the first two players selected next spring — even if it requires another team trading up to get him. 3. New York Jets: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State I like the veteran additions made by the Jets (on both sides of the ball) and expect the club’s native first-round pick to be much lower than No. 3 overall. That said, with two other first-round picks added via trades, the Jets have the firepower to do whatever they want. With all due respect to the quarterbacks, Smith is arguably the best player in this class, with a frame, speed and star power similar to a young Julio Jones. 4. Cleveland Browns: Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina The 2027 first-round selection the Browns received from the Rams in the Myles Garrett trade won’t come until much later on Day 1, but with the top quarterbacks off the board and several blue-chip defensive prospects available, Cleveland should be satisfied with reloading on that side of the ball with this pick. Stewart’s blend of burst, bend and length is the building blocks of a future All-Pro. Adding him to a defensive line already featuring Jared Verse and Mason Graham would be exciting. 5. Las Vegas Raiders: Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame Based on the investment made this past spring in No. 1 overall selection Fernando Mendoza and veteran Kirk Cousins, new head coach Klint Kubiak may very well push for a wide receiver (Cam Coleman?) with the Raiders’ top choice. But it would be hard to pass up a talent like Moore here. He's right with Derek Stingley and Patrick Surtain II as one of the cleanest cornerback prospects I’ve evaluated over the past decade. Moore combines size, agility, instincts and ball skills to project as a future NFL star. 6. Atlanta Falcons: Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas Perhaps the Falcons will be feeling better about their edge group a year from now, but with James Pearce Jr. out for half the season (suspension) and Jalon Walker out for the entire season (torn ACL), the club has little choice but to have contingency plans. A former linebacker turned edge rusher following a similar path as Arvell Reese and Micah Parsons, Simmons is a one-man wrecking crew who could fix what currently ails Atlanta’s pass rush. 7. Tennessee Titans: Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas The Titans invested a lot of money ($82 million over four years) in left tackle Dan Moore Jr., and the results last year were typical of what he’d shown earlier in his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers — he surrendered eight sacks over 16 regular-season games. If picking this high, the Titans could see Goosby as an upgrade as Cam Ward’s blindside protector. Goosby put a scare into the Longhorns (and scouts) by going down with a knee injury in August, but he reportedly suffered a bone bruise that should take just weeks, not months, to heal. Goosby was fantastic last season, but it was his first as a starter. If he can build upon it, he has the talent to be the first offensive lineman drafted this spring. 8. Carolina Panthers: Cam Coleman, WR, Texas Four Longhorns among the first eight selections of the 2027 NFL draft? It could happen, which is a big reason why Texas is my pick to win the national title this year. An acrobatic one-handed grab shared on social media from camp this summer had fans gushing, but scouts have been tracking Coleman since he flashed at Auburn. A springy athlete with excellent size and tracking skills, Coleman reminds me a lot of another star wideout playing in Texas: Cowboys star George Pickens. Pairing Coleman with reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan would give the Panthers the opportunity to better evaluate Bryce Young in what will be the last year of his rookie contract. 9. New Orleans Saints: Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia I like the Saints’ young nucleus in the secondary, but GM Mickey Loomis has been doing this too long to think he wouldn’t consider adding another premier cover corner, if available. Robinson isn’t as big or as physical as the aforementioned Leonard Moore, but he possesses elite agility, acceleration and ball skills. 10. New York Giants: A’Mauri Washington, DT, Oregon Trading away Dexter Lawrence left a massive hole in the middle of John Harbaugh’s defense, and I think he’ll prioritize replacing him in the draft. Washington may not have the statistics (33 tackles, including 4.5 for loss and 1.5 sacks in 2026) one normally associates with a first-round selection, but had he entered the 2026 draft, I believe he would’ve joined Caleb Banks (Minnesota) and Peter Woods (Kansas City) as a Day 1 pick. Football is a big man’s game, and Washington has rare quickness for his 6-foot-3, 330-pound frame. 11. Washington Commanders: Trey'Dez Green, TE, LSU We are all eager to see Jayden Daniels back on the field, but unless the Commanders surround him with more dynamic pass-catchers, Daniels might remain largely a one-man show on offense. Call Green a wide receiver or a tight end, the 6-foot-7, 240-pound target is a matchup nightmare. 12. New York Jets (from Colts): Will Echoles, DT, Mississippi It would be fascinating if the Jets use the selection gained in the Sauce Gardner trade on a cornerback, but replacing defensive lineman Quinnen Williams on the inside should be an even higher priority. Echoles isn’t as stout at the point of attack as Williams, but he’s cat-quick and passionate, playing with the high-revving motor Aaron Glenn would appreciate. 13. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Trevor Lauck, OL, Iowa The Bucs showed clear vision back in 2020 with the selection of Tristan Wirfs out of Iowa and could return to the deepest well for offensive linemen in college football with Lauck, whose lack of ideal length and foot speed could push him inside to guard in the NFL. Big, powerful and technically sound, Lauck is arguably the "safest" of this year’s offensive line prospects. A big contract will certainly be the most important factor in bringing Baker Mayfield back, but boosting the offensive line wouldn’t hurt. 14. Minnesota Vikings: Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State The Vikings surprised some during the 2026 draft with the gamble on uber-talented but inconsistent defensive tackle Caleb Banks. I could see defensive coordinator Brian Flores pushing for a similarly unique prospect in Jones at cornerback. The 6-foot-4, 196-pound Jones allowed a total of 11 receptions last season, corralling receivers with his long arms and shockingly light feet. New general manager Nolan Teasley saw a lot of success in Seattle with oversized cornerbacks and might also be willing to bet big on Jones’ potential. 15. Pittsburgh Steelers: Sammy Brown, LB, Clemson Patrick Queen is entering the final season of a three-year, $41 million contract. Brown — an All-ACC honoree after each of his first two seasons at Clemson — plays with similar speed at a much lower salary. 16. Jacksonville Jaguars: Chris Cole, LB, Georgia The Jaguars saw Devin Lloyd leave for Carolina (and $45 million) in free agency and could be targeting a cheaper (and more versatile) replacement in the 2027 draft. The 6-foot-3, 235-pound Cole has been moved all over Georgia’s defense the past two seasons, so he doesn’t have the stats to suggest he’ll be a first-round pick. But his raw athleticism has scouts projecting him as one of this year’s breakout stars. 17. Chicago Bears: Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU Few teams bet on traits like the Bears, and Seaton is as gifted as there is. The biggest question about the former five-star recruit concerns the level of competition he faced at Colorado the past two seasons. The 6-foot-5, 307-pound Seaton boasts rare quickness and agility. If he passes the SEC test, he has a chance to be the first blocker taken next year, and long off the board by this point. 18. New York Jets (from Cowboys): CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame Armed with three first-round picks in a class widely expected to boast a rich quarterback crop, Jets general manager Darren Mougey probably would get run out of town if he didn’t invest a single Day 1 pick on the game’s most important position. Carr is an intriguing fit for New York because he showed exciting awareness and accuracy as a first-year starter last year for Notre Dame and is perhaps better prepared for the mental rigors of playing in the Big Apple — given the scrutiny he’s endured with the Irish along with being the grandson of former Michigan head coach Lloyd Carr. 19. Cincinnati Bengals: KJ Bolden, S, Georgia The Bengals traditionally use their first-round selections on big, fast athletes with high ceilings, but they might make an exception with Bolden. Officially listed by Georgia at 6-0, 195 pounds, Bolden is slighter than most teams want at safety, but his instincts, physicality and closing speed pop off the tape. 20. Denver Broncos: Jamari Johnson, TE, Oregon The Broncos boast one of the NFL’s most well-rounded rosters, and I think they’ll be picking later than DraftKings’ current projection. Even after investing a couple of Day 3 picks on tight ends in 2026, the position remains one of the few that I think Denver could use reinforcement. Remember, veterans Evan Engram and Lucas Krull are impending free agents. Johnson was overshadowed by Kenyon Sadiq at Oregon last year, but he's one of my favorite breakout candidates this season. 21. Houston Texans: Bryant Wesco Jr., WR, Clemson Catastrophic injuries to Tank Dell and now Jayden Higgins are compromising the Texans' passing attack and stunting the development of young quarterback C.J. Stroud. Rather than banking on a return to health from the undeniably talented pass-catchers already on the roster, GM Nick Caserio may opt to add to the room. A Texas native who inherited his parents’ track-star speed, Wesco could be a perfect fit for Houston. 22. Detroit Lions: Cade Pieper, C, Iowa With expected starting center Cade Maye fracturing his wrist in training camp, Detroit GM Brad Holmes might wish that he could invest his club’s 2027 first-round pick on Pieper right now. It isn’t often that teams are willing to select centers in the first round, but if Pieper’s transition to center (from right guard) this season goes as expected, he’ll earn it. He's the most intriguing interior offensive lineman of this class. 23. Los Angeles Chargers: Jyaire Hill, CB, Michigan Recruited by Jim Harbaugh to Michigan, Hill could be traveling west to rejoin his former head coach. The 6-foot-2, 189-pound Hill doesn’t have the gaudy statistics one normally associates with first-round cornerbacks (two career interceptions), but his length and physicality project well to the next level and I think he’ll flourish under Kyle Whittingham in Ann Arbor this fall. 24. San Francisco 49ers: Yhonzae Pierre, Edge, Alabama Everyone knows that Nick Bosa is one of the NFL’s elite edge rushers, but he’s missed a lot of action over his career and is coming off a third torn ACL. Whether it be to complement Bosa or plan for the future, the 49ers must invest in more pass-rushers, and Pierre has both the twitch and toughness that would fit well with their current bunch. 25. Kansas City Chiefs: Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana There have been more flashes than consistency from top Kansas City receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy since they entered the NFL in 2023 and 2024, respectively. Perhaps it all comes together for one (or both) this year. If not, Becker is a polished route-runner and hands-catcher whose dependability could be especially coveted by the Chiefs. 26. Dallas Cowboys (from Packers): Kewan Lacy, RB, Ole Miss I’m a believer in Javonte Williams and head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s offense, but I think the Cowboys will consider adding more juice to their backfield in the near future. It isn’t often that NFL teams are willing to invest a first-round pick on a running back who weighs less than 200 pounds, but Lacy led the SEC with 306 touches and 24 rushing touchdowns a year ago. Some scouts believe he is the second coming of De’Von Achane. 27. New England Patriots: Tae Johnson, S, Notre Dame As one might expect of the defending AFC champs, the Patriots boast one of the league’s most complete rosters. Depth at safety is a question, however, especially with veterans Kevin Byard and Mike Brown approaching free agency. Johnson has size (6-foot-2, 195 pounds), speed and ball-hawking skills. 28. Philadelphia Eagles: Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson Yes, the Eagles boast reigning All-Pros Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean at cornerback, but both will be seeking a big payday soon enough, while fellow projected starter Riq Woolen is on a one-year deal. The 6-foot-3, 204-pound Hampton looks the part of a future NFL star and has flashy tape, but his technique is inconsistent. Given all the talent in Philly, this defense could be the perfect spot for him to blossom. 29. Baltimore Ravens: Austin Siereveld, OL, Ohio State Siereveld was the Buckeyes’ starting left tackle a year ago and plays with surprising balance at 6-foot-5, 325 pounds. I think he might be even better inside at guard or center due to his broad, powerful frame. 30. Seattle Seahawks: Matayo Uiagalelei, Edge, Oregon A fearsome "Darkside" defense powered the Seahawks’ Super Bowl run, but reinforcements are needed on the edge. DeMarcus Lawrence has already announced that this will be his final season in the NFL, while Uchenna Nwosu (who turns 30 in December) is in the final year of his deal. Enter the 6-foot-5, 265-pound Uiagalelei? He wins against the pass and the run with his length, power and pro-ready technique. 31. Buffalo Bills: Ahmad Moten, DT, Miami Ed Oliver was limited to just three games a season ago due to injury and is grieving the tragic drowning of his 2-year-old son. Buffalo is another situation where the general manager might wish he could use his 2027 first-round pick on a more immediate contributor at a specific position. Should the Bills wait until the draft, adding Moten would make a lot of sense. While he needs to prove that last year’s breakout was not merely the byproduct of opponents focusing heavily on 2026 first-round edge rushers Rueben Bain Jr. (Bucs) and Akheem Mesidor (Chargers), Moten has all the traits to earn first-round consideration. 32. Cleveland Browns (from Rams): Sam Leavitt, QB, LSU For decades, Browns fans have wished their beloved team would earn the final first-round pick of a given NFL draft. Well, having acquired the Rams' first-rounder in the Myles Garrett trade might finally provide the opportunity. In the interest of securing the No. 32 pick via winning the Super Bowl, Cleveland will almost certainly target a quarterback on Day 1 of the 2027 draft. One intriguing option is Leavitt, who flashed at Arizona State and I believe will flourish at LSU with Lane Kiffin.

articles.title: “Unbelievable things coming soon": Patrick and Brittany Mahomes take their family brand to the next level with new campaign
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is adding a distinctly personal touch to his growing off-field profile. With the new NFL season approaching, the Kansas City Chiefs qu.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is adding a distinctly personal touch to his growing off-field profile. With the new NFL season approaching, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has offered fans a first look at a campaign that brings Brittany Mahomes and their three children into the frame. The move highlights how the Mahomes name is becoming more than a football identity, with family, business and entertainment increasingly shaping the quarterback’s public image.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes bring family into new campaignMahomes shared a short teaser for the upcoming project, titled “Unbelievable,” giving fans a glimpse of himself with Brittany and their children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden.“Unbelievable things coming soon,” Mahomes wrote while sharing the teaser.The message was brief, but the image behind it carried plenty of meaning. Instead of another campaign built around Mahomes alone, the quarterback has chosen to put his entire immediate family at the center of the latest project.That approach fits the way the Mahomes brand has evolved. Patrick remains one of the NFL’s biggest stars, but Brittany has also created a strong public identity of her own through her business interests, sports involvement and social media presence.Their children have also become familiar faces in the family’s public content. The new campaign takes that family visibility a step further by placing all three children alongside their parents in a commercial setting.The timing is also significant. Mahomes is entering his 10th NFL season, a milestone that underlines how much his career and public profile have grown since he became Kansas City’s starting quarterback.Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes expands his off-field brandMahomes has spent years building a profile that stretches well beyond football. articles.title: Panthers in same Super Bowl tier as Buccaneers, Falcons, Saints
articles.summary: All four teams in the NFC South, at least according to CBS Sports' Super Bowl tiers, are standing on the same ground at the start of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The NFC South isn't exactly the cream of the NFL's crop.

In 2025, and for the first time in a decade, the Carolina Panthers won the division . . . at 8-9 . . . and with a -69 point differential. And going into 2026, the outlook for the reigning champs, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the Atlanta Falcons and the New Orleans Saints doesn't appear too bright.

All four of the NFC South's teams landed in the same Super Bowl tier in CBS Sports' new power rankings by Carter Bahns. Bahns writes:

The C Tier might be the most fluid. If everything clicks for these teams, they can clinch a spot in the playoffs. If it falls apart, they could bottom out and face tough questions about whether to keep their coaching staff and whether to blow up their rosters. Nothing exemplifies that reality quite like the NFC South. All four teams landed in this tier for two reasons. One, they are all on equal footing, as evidenced by the three-way tie atop the division in 2025. Two, none of them are particularly great, which showed in all of them finishing last season under .500.

It's tough to argue that any of these four teams belong in a higher tier.

Atlanta has some of the most talented players in the division, but is also dealing with the worst quarterback situation of the bunch.

Tampa Bay has some great pieces like defensive lineman Vita Vea and second-year receiver Emeka Egbuka. But with quarterback Baker Mayfield and the organization at an impasse over his next contract, their run could soon be coming to an end.

New Orleans could have the most promising quarterback in the division after a very impressive rookie season from Tyler Shough. However, it's going to take a while for them to climb out of the hole they dug for themselves by keeping the Drew Brees-era roster together for far too long after he left.

The Panthers are a wild card based on what they get or don't get from their quarterback, Bryce Young. It's conceivable that they could finish anywhere between 10 wins and five wins, depending on how he does as well as the health of their key pieces.

Bottom line—nobody really knows what to expect from this division.

articles.body:
NFL executives shared mixed opinions on whether Drake Maye will be able to lead the New England Patriots back to another Super Bowl in a new survey published by The Athletic's Mike Sando .

The Buffalo Bills performed the best in Sando's survey, with four of six participating NFL executives ranking Josh Allen's squad as the best team in the AFC.

The Denver Broncos (second overall) and Houston Texans (third overall) also received votes as the conference's best team, according to Sando.

49ers DE's Hilarious Plan for Australia Flight

The Patriots averaged fourth place overall but received a wider range of rankings, with one executive ranking the team third in the AFC and another sliding the team all the way down to ninth.

Multiple executives speaking with Sando pointed out the Patriots' favorable schedule last season as a reason to expect Maye and his team to take a step back in 2026.

One executive described the Patriots to Sando as "the No. 1 regression team."

The Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs were ranked fifth and sixth overall, respectively, according to Sando. Executives speaking with Sando expressed doubts about the health of both Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes.

The choice for the lowest-ranked club in the AFC was almost unanimous, per Sando. Five out of six executives surveyed by Sando expect the Miami Dolphins to be the worst team in the conference after coach Jeff Hafley told reporters he won't measure success this season by winning.

The Patriots will get the chance to improve their championship odds when opening the season on the road next Wednesday against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks.

C.J. Stroud and the Texans are set to open their own campaign the following Sunday against the visiting Bills, the day before Bo Nix and the Broncos visit the Chiefs in what could be Mahomes' return from knee surgery.

articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers announced plans Thursday for a weeklong celebration across Pittsburgh leading up to their regular season opener against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 at Acrisure Stadium.

The Steelers Kickoff Week activities will feature community events and interactive displays across six local neighborhoods.

At the center of the celebration is a traveling display featuring giant Super Bowl rings originally created for the 2026 NFL Draft Steelers Country activation.

From Monday through Saturday of game week, the giant Super Bowl rings will visit six different locations across Pittsburgh. At each stop, fans will be invited to participate in a paint-by-numbers project by painting a segment of a larger canvas representing that location.

Once completed, the six individual pieces will be assembled into a single 24-foot mural. The completed artwork will be unveiled to fans at Acrisure Stadium during the team's home opener.

Along the tour route, the Steelers will also host a series of charity and community events in the participating neighborhoods. Steelers Vice President of Strategy Dan Rooney noted that the team designed the activities to maintain connection with local supporters following the city's hosting of the draft.

"What drives the Steelers is our fans," Rooney said. "That's why we're bringing kickoff week excitement directly to them. After welcoming the football world to Pittsburgh for the 2026 NFL Draft, we're taking a piece of that experience into neighborhoods across the city — giving fans a chance to relive the historic event, connect with our team's legacy and build excitement for the season ahead."

Monday, 9/7: Patricia Rooney Memorial Fountain in Allegheny Commons Park, North Side

This location will also kick off a week-long matching campaign benefiting the Salvation Army Harbor Light Center in recognition of the 40th anniversary of Project Bundle-Up, which Patricia Rooney helped to pioneer.

Tuesday, 9/8: U.S. Steel Community Field at Hazelwood Green, Hazelwood

This location will also host a free Steelers Youth Football Mini Camp for youth ages 6-14 from 6:30-8 p.m.

The Oakland stop brings Kickoff Week to the city's college community, just blocks from the former site of Forbes Field, where the Steelers played their first home game in 1933.

Thursday, 9/10: Lawn of Point State Park, Downtown

The rings return to one of Pittsburgh's most iconic locations, Point State Park, where they were first displayed as part of Steelers Country during the 2026 NFL Draft.

Friday, 9/11: Acrisure Stadium, North Shore

To mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, volunteers will join a nationwide movement to "Honor Through Action." As part of the largest annual day of service in U.S. history, volunteers will pack more than 248,500 healthy, non-perishable meals for local families at risk of hunger. All meals packed will be donated to the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank for distribution to local individuals and families in need.

Saturday, 9/12: Duquesne Incline Overlook, Mt. Washington

The Steelers will cover Duquesne Incline fares from 12-2 p.m.

Sunday, 9/13: Kickoff Game, Steelers vs. Falcons at Acrisure Stadium

All six Super Bowl rings and the completed fan-painted mural will arrive at Acrisure Stadium as the week-long journey culminates on gameday.

Paul’s comments add more fuel to a feud that has already spilled from the field into public confrontations and social media exchanges.Logan Paul makes fresh claim about Tom Brady and flag football gamePaul revisited the rivalry while speaking with Valuetainment for Gen Z’s Patrick Bet-David, where he described Brady as someone who had singled him out during their meeting on the flag football field.“For some reason, I’ve become Tom Brady’s target, which is something I just can’t accept. I’m not going to stand here and be belittled by you in front of everyone at the flag football draft. I’m not going to let you disrespect me in the middle of the game by doing a cheap shot at me,” Logan told Valuetainment for Gen Z’s Patrick Bet-David.He then made a stronger accusation about the officials involved in the game.“And then he probably paid the refs or something because they called the penalty on me. So there’s fraud right there. And then, him actually assaulting me and striking me … at the end of the day, it’s like, why me? Why have you chosen me? Why have you chosen me? And so, you want war, you’ll get war, brother.”Paul’s comments refer to the Fanatics Flag Football Classic, where he played for the Wildcats against Brady’s Founders team. The event brought together NFL stars and the U.S. men’s national flag football team, creating a competitive setting that also carried plenty of entertainment value.The Wildcats defeated Brady’s team during the tournament, although Team USA eventually claimed the title. articles.title: Baker Mayfield Called More 'Relatable' Than Tom Brady by Bucs GM Jason Licht
articles.summary: Although he has yet to reach the same level of success in the NFL, there is a belief within the Tampa Bay Buccaneers organization that quarterback Baker Mayfield is easier to relate to than his predecessor, Tom Brady.
articles.body:
Although he has yet to reach the same level of success in the NFL, there is a belief within the Tampa Bay Buccaneers organization that quarterback Baker Mayfield is easier to relate to than his predecessor, Tom Brady.

Bucs general manager Jason Licht made the declaration to The Athletic's Zak Keefer (h/t The Athletic's Emily Ohman ), saying, "I would never throw shade on Tom because I like my ring too much, but Baker is just more … relatable."

Offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs, who is Mayfield's closest friend on the Bucs, seemed to agree, saying, "Tom really didn't do anything with us, because he couldn't. Like, he couldn't even go to dinner. Then Baker comes in, and the first day he's here he asks me if I wanna grab a beer that night. I'm like, 'This is sick!'"

Per Keefer (h/t Ohman), Mayfield does many things that endear him to his teammates, ranging from playing video games and chugging beers to paying for their visits with his personal physiotherapist.

Brady spent the final three years of his career with the Bucs, and he enjoyed enormous success, leading them to a Super Bowl victory.

When Brady retired at the end of the 2022 season, the Buccaneers' quarterback situation was very much in question, so they rolled the dice on signing Mayfield in free agency.

Mayfield, who was fresh off failed runs with the Cleveland Browns and Carolina Panthers, proceeded to win the starting job, and he never looked back.

Over his three seasons in Tampa, Mayfield has posted a 27-24 record, leading the Bucs to the playoffs twice. He has also completed 66.3 percent of his passes for 12,237 yards, 95 touchdowns and 37 interceptions en route to two Pro Bowl selections.

Mayfield, who is entering a contract year, will look to get the Buccaneers back on track in 2026 after they missed the playoffs last season.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Deep Sleepers Based on Latest Rankings
articles.summary: Barring injuries, most early picks in a fantasy football draft are going to be hits.
articles.body:
Barring injuries, most early picks in a fantasy football draft are going to be hits.

So, when you're looking to build an edge over your rival league mates, you need to find value later in the draft.

Luckily, it is readily available. Every NFL season spawns a new batch of surprisingly productive players.

You just have to know where to find them. And we're here to simplify that process by spotlighting a couple of deep sleepers who won't cost you a top 125 pick after laying out our latest PPR rankings.

Keaton Mitchell, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Assuming Mitchell's latest injury issue is nothing major (and it sounds like that's the case ), he could be primed for his best NFL season to date—by a mile.

He can add explosion to this offense. With burst like this, he only needs a sliver of space to turn any touch into a big play. And with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel at the controls, there could be actual hallways opening in front of Mitchell.

Even if he's only handling the lightning duty behind the thunder that is Omarion Hampton, Mitchell could strike often enough to serve as a legitimate flex option. And should Hampton happen to miss any time, Mitchell might immediately rocket into RB2 territory.

This past season, Mitchell's average touch spanned 5.9 yards. As a rookie in 2023, that number landed at a whopping 8.7. He might not be quite that efficient with a heavily increased role, but if he's consistently barreling long balls and legging out extra-base hits, he might do more in a supporting role than some do with a featured gig.

A third-round rookie out of USC, Lane ranked as one of the NFL's true head-turners during training camp and preseason. There is absolutely a chance those flashes were simply the appetizer to a true regular-season feast.

Baltimore needs more pass-catching playmakers than Zay Flowers, and Lane looks like the most electric option to fill that void. He can stretch the field as a long-striding deep-ball threat, and he might be even more effective in the red zone as a 6'4" mismatch with a massive catch radius and great hands.

Over three seasons with the Trojans, Lane's average reception covered 13.8 yards. In 2024, he tallied 12 touchdowns on only 43 catches.

There might be peaks and valleys with his production, but his good games could be matchup-deciders. His best-case scenarios look pretty special and just might include Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

The star pass rusher, now with the Los Angeles Rams, was voted No. 1 overall in the NFL's Top 100 rankings on Thursday. He was voted No. 8 in 2025.

Allen, 30, is coming off another tremendous season in which he racked up 3,668 yards, 25 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while rushing for 579 yards and 14 touchdowns.

The Bills finished the season 12-5, losing in the divisional round to the Denver Broncos in overtime.

One of the most creative players, perhaps in league history, Allen is able to beat defenders over the top with deep shots while also finding receivers on short passes after plays break down.

At 6'5", 237 pounds, Allen can also run through and around defenders as well as any quarterback in the NFL today.

The 2024 MVP is sure to put together a strong campaign in 2026, but the biggest knock against Allen is his lack of postseason success. He and the Bills have yet to make it past the AFC Championship Game, often falling short to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs.

Last year seemed like the best chance Allen has had to reach the Super Bowl since the Chiefs missed the playoffs, but Buffalo ultimately fell short to the Broncos.

A championship ring is the only thing keeping Allen from being in the same conversation with some of the all-time greats, and he'll look to get over the hump this year.

Garrett earning the top spot should come as no surprise given the season he just had.

The 30-year-old proved that he's only getting better with age as he completely wrecked opposing offensive lines on his way to the NFL's single-season sack record.

Garrett finished the 2025 campaign with 23 sacks, breaking the previous record of 22.5, held by Michael Strahan (2001) and T.J. Watt (2021). Garrett's previous career high for sacks was 16, so he reached a completely different level last season.

While Garrett was by far the most impactful defensive player in the NFL last season, it really didn't mean that much since he was on a lowly Cleveland Browns team that finished 5-12.

This year, it's a completely different story.

The Rams made the biggest move of the offseason when they acquired Garrett for linebacker Jared Verse and a haul of draft picks. Los Angeles already boasted one of the best offenses in the NFL, and bringing in Garrett quickly made the Rams the team to watch to win it all in 2026.

To make matters worse for opposing offenses, legendary defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of retirement to join Garrett on the defensive line, meaning Los Angeles went from having a middling defense in 2025 to one of the best heading into this season.

articles.title: Raiders Secure $75M in Public Funding For $158M Allegiant Stadium Upgrade Plan

articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders have made major progress in their goal of upgrading Allegiant Stadium.

Per the Associated Press , the Las Vegas Stadium Authority approved $75 million in public funds towards the $158 million upgrade to the stadium. The team will take on the rest of the cost to improve Allegiant Stadium.

"Allegiant Stadium is a critical community asset," said Steve Hill, president and CEO of the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority. "It is driving tourism right now more than ever at a time we need to drive tourism. We all know that the tourism drives the economy. Keeping that stadium at its current level is a high priority for all of us. It is the requirement and the law, but it's very important for our community."

The funds acquired on Wednesday specifically will go towards improving the path into the north entrance of the 65,000-seat stadium, which cost $2 billion to build and opened in 2020.

"The north side of the building has become one of the more pressure points in the guest experience," Raiders president Sandra Douglass Morgan said. "That infrastructure is stretched to capacity."

According to the AP, construction on the project isn't expected to start until after the 2026 season, and the team is aiming for a completion date in late 2028 or before the 2029 Super Bowl, which will be hosted by Allegiant Stadium.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson's Depth Chart Standing Revealed by Colts' Shane Steichen After Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Anthony Richardson has beaten out Riley Leonard for the Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback job despite seeking a trade earlier this offseason.
articles.body:
Anthony Richardson has beaten out Riley Leonard for the Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback job despite seeking a trade earlier this offseason.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters Thursday Richardson will serve as QB2 behind Daniel Jones.

"I thought he did some good things through camp. He's continued to develop and grow and learn and continue to get better, and same thing with Riley," Steichen said Thursday (h/t 107.5 The Fan's Kevin Bowen).

Richardson told reporters he is "extremely grateful" for the opportunity, adding, "I love adversity. I love life."

He also addressed his earlier trade request.

"When I reported back for OTAs, I was here, told myself I was going to be here and prepare myself like I was going to be here for the start of the season," Richardson said.

Jones is set to start Week 1 for the Colts after joining training camp as a full participant following recovery from the ruptured Achilles tendon he suffered last December.

The news comes after Richardson's agent told ESPN's Stephen Holder in February the Colts had given his client permission to seek a trade.

Richardson said in early August he hadn't recently discussed the trade request with either his agent or general manager Chris Ballard.

Asked about what would happen if the Colts didn't trade him, Richardson said last month, "If that's what the team wants, that's what I want. I just want go be able to help a team."

Ballard said Tuesday he was expecting Richardson to still be with the Colts this season.

"We forget how young he is sometimes," Ballard said earlier this week. "I'm really proud of his growth... there was times in camp that I said, 'Okay, he's starting to really show some poise.'"

Jones has gotten the majority of first-team reps throughout camp as Richardson and Leonard split work with the Colts' second and third units.

"Consistency, that's going to be part of their job going through this season," Steichen said Thursday about his backup quarterbacks. "Getting those scout team reps, that's going to be big for them, because you never know when their number could get called."

Richardson started 15 games for the Colts across his first two NFL seasons while missing significant time to injury in both campaigns.

He competed to keep his QB1 role last summer before losing the job to Jones.

The former No. 4 overall pick's first season as Jones' backup was once again impacted by injuries. Richardson suffered an orbital fracture in an October accident involving stretching bands and did not see any playing time from Week 6 onward.

Richardson is heading into the final season of his rookie deal after the Colts declined his 2027 fifth-year option. Whether he sees any playing time will depend in part on Jones' health as the starting quarterback prepares to make his return from injury Sunday, Sept. 13 against the visiting Baltimore Ravens.

articles.title: Examining Fantasy Football 2026 Expert Mock Drafts After Preseason Week 3
articles.summary: The end of the 2026 NFL preseason sent the fantasy football world into the heart of mock draft season.
articles.body:
The end of the 2026 NFL preseason sent the fantasy football world into the heart of mock draft season.

It feels a little differently than it has in the past due to the proliferation of simulated mock drafts. It can be hard clearing out schedule space for 10 to 12 experts to mock together, so many aren't bothering.

However, there are still fantasy crews who are mock drafting together, so we'll look at three of the latest offerings, analyzing shared trends and notable differences from a 10-team mock at ESPN, a 12-team mock at ESPN and a 12-team mock from FanSided.

For simplicity's sake, let's compare the first rounds of the two 12-team mocks with the first 12 picks made during the 10-teamer. While there are some clear similarities, there are notable differences, too.

The first takeaway: If you want Gibbs or Robinson, you better have a top-two pick in hand. Nothing was surprising about their prominent placement, including the fact that there wasn't universal agreement on the order of them.

The second: First-round values feel pretty well defined. Despite only presenting a dozen picks, all three draft boards agreed on 10 different players. If you're bracing yourself for a curveball, this isn't where you're likely to find it.

The final: How about those disagreements? Among the five players who weren't universal first-round picks, only one (Walker) showed up on multiple draft boards. Otherwise, it was one-and-done showings for Achane, Henry, Jefferson and Barkley.

The NFL's most important position is perhaps the fantasy world's most polarizing.

The general feeling among fantasy experts is that elite quarterbacks aren't worth the opportunity cost of spending such a premium pick on them. Since most leagues only start one signal-caller, the thinking goes that the player pool is deep enough to have serviceable-or-better starters available for everyone.

Given that these were expert mocks, they sort of all devalued the quarterback position together. None of the mocks featured a quarterback taken in the top two rounds, and only FanSided's had a quarterback crack the first three rounds (Josh Allen, 25th). In ESPN's 12-teamer, Allen didn't come off the board until the 46th pick.

To help highlight the position's depth, managers didn't need a top-100 pick to collect QB12. The 12th quarterbacks taken were Patrick Mahomes at No. 120 (in ESPN's 12-teamer), Caleb Williams (No. 110 in the 10-teamer) and Kyler Murray (No. 104 at FanSided).

Anytime I'm tasked with presenting mock draft advice, one tip always makes the cut: Run through multiple mocks. While things like average draft position and consensus rankings might present a sense of groupthink, there are always eye-catching deviations in any draft room you'll find.

In this exercise, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels looms as a pretty large one. In the two ESPN mocks, he was QB2 and a fifth-round pick (going at Nos. 50 and 54). Over at FanSided, though, he was only QB5 and lasted until near the end of the sixth round (No. 69).

FanSided, meanwhile, was highest on Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley, who landed eighth overall. At ESPN, he made it to picks Nos. 14 and 19. It was also lowest on Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, a mid-third-round pick there (No. 29), but a comfortable second-round pick at ESPN (Nos. 15 and 18).

Similar disagreements continued throughout the mocks, serving as a reminder that any draft room can turn upon the whims of any manager involved. And if a deviation starts a position run, it's up to you to decide whether to get in on the feeding frenzy or leave it alone to look for bargains elsewhere.

articles.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo Says He Considered Retiring After Gruesome Season-Ending Injury as Rookie
articles.summary: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo divulged Thursday that he thought about stepping away from football after his rookie season.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo divulged Thursday that he thought about stepping away from football after his rookie season.

When asked by Kay Adams on Up & Adams if he considered retirement after suffering a fractured tibia, ruptured deltoid ligament and dislocated right ankle last season, Skattebo confirmed that he did (beginning at the 1:10 mark of the video) :

"Yeah, definitely," Skattebo said. "I would say probably a month in, like the first month, I was like, 'Damn, do I really wanna do this?' And then, it was seven games. I was like, 'I gotta go back and play.' There's no shot. If it was the end of the year and I was like, 'Okay, I'm over this.' I didn't feel that way at all. ... I think that gave me an extra step of finding that deep place and coming out of a hole that I didn't know I could come out of."

At the start of the video, Skattebo noted that he told himself before he entered the NFL that he would stop playing in the event of a major injury, saying, "Coming out of college, going into the NFL, I think I gave myself one rule. And that was if I ever got a major injury, I was done playing. And that happened seven games into my career, so it kind of sucked. But I think that really helped me find who I am as a player and a person."

Despite his uncertainty about continuing to play after the injury, Skattebo ultimately decided to keep going, and he appears ready for a full workload in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular-season against the Dallas Cowboys after playing during the preseason.

After the Giants selected Skattebo in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL draft out of Arizona State, he began his rookie campaign as a backup.

However, he quickly seized the starting job and proceeded to rush for 308 yards and three touchdowns, while also catching 14 passes for 120 yards and two scores over his five starts.

Skattebo was trending toward being in the Offensive Rookie of the Year conversation, but his momentum came to a halt in Week 8 against the Philadelphia Eagles when he suffered numerous injuries that ended his season prematurely.

New York overhauled its coaching staff after finishing just 4-13, but it could prove to be a hugely positive development for Skattebo and the Giants' running game as a whole.

New head coach John Harbaugh consistently deployed an elite rushing attack during his time with the Baltimore Ravens, finishing no worse than third in the NFL in rushing in each of the past eight seasons.

Baltimore ranked first in rushing four times during that stretch, including 2024 when the combination of running back Derrick Henry and quarterback Lamar Jackson ran rampant.

Skattebo and quarterback Jaxson Dart perhaps have a chance to be a version of that in 2026, particularly if Harbaugh commits to Skattebo as his unquestioned, No. 1 guy in the backfield.

Although Skattebo may have to contend with the likes of Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary for touches, there is no question that Skattebo is the most talented of the bunch, and he has a chance to pick up where he left off before the injury.

articles.title: Rams' Myles Garrett tops NFL's 'Top 100' list, edging out No. 2 Josh Allen
articles.summary: Garrett finished ahead of No. 2 Josh Allen, becoming just the third defensive player to top the top 100.
articles.body:
The "NFL Top 100" voters have spoken: Myles Garrett is the best player in the NFL.

Garrett, the Rams' new superstar pass rusher, has become just the third defender in the TV show's 16-year history to win the award. The first was J.J. Watt in 2015. The other was Garrett's new Rams teammate, Aaron Donald, in 2019.

After dropping from No. 11 to No. 20 following the 2022 season, Garrett rose to fifth in 2024 and placed eighth on last year's list. All Garrett did last season for the lowly Browns was break the league's single-season sack record with 23 (in 17 games), winning Defensive Player of the Year and being named first-team All-Pro.

The Browns traded Garrett to the Rams for Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and a conditional 2029 conditional selection.

Bills QB Josh Allen finished second, followed by Falcons RB Bijan Robinson. The rest of the top 10, in descending order: Rams QB Matthew Stafford, Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey, Rams WR Puka Nacua, Packers EDGE Micah Parsons, Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs and Broncos CB Patrick Surtain II.

Is this one of the less controversial 'Top 100' No. 1 picks?

The votes are often highly scrutinized and, as the results show, strongly slanted toward offensive players at the very top. Quarterbacks have finished atop the list nine times in total, although the past two winners before Garrett were non-QBs: Tyreek Hill in 2024 and Saquon Barkley in 2025.

But perhaps the voters got this one right this time around.

Garrett's 2025 season will go down as one of the greatest individual defensive campaigns in recent memory, especially considering the circumstances. The Browns went 5-12, with six losses by double digits. It's no shock why the Rams paid a premium for Garrett ahead of his age-31 season — and why the Rams, with firepower on both sides of the ball, are considered the odds-on favorite to win Super Bowl LXI prior to the 2026 season.

You hear in the way opponents talk about Garrett. They see him as a rare specimen, uniquely qualified to mess up opposing offenses. His get-off and burst remain elite. Blockers measure their self-worth based on matchups against Garrett, even if they receive help. Offenses almost never block him straight up and just run their normal stuff without accounting for him.

That's impact . Sure, the 23 sacks are likely what pushed Garrett ahead of Allen this year. Had the Bills won the Super Bowl, well, perhaps the vote would have been slightly different. That's not to say that Buffalo winning a few more playoff games would have rendered Allen a slightly better player, but that optics do matter in these types of votes.

Garrett earned the spot, which you can't always say is true. Barkley was hardly a consensus selection a year ago. Hill finishing first two years ago might have been the biggest jumped-the-shark moment in the Top 100 history.

Other wild things have happened, like Lamar Jackson going from completely unranked the year before to No. 1 in 2020 or Cam Newton topping the list in 2016 (after being 73rd the year before). This year feels about as solid and accurate as it has been in recent years, even Allen's legion of fans might strongly push back.

Not everyone will agree with Garrett at the top, of course. But this just feels like the right time and place for him to break through to the top. If the Rams go on to win the Super Bowl, with Garrett having the impact they hope, it would only justify the rankings even more.

articles.title: Athletic's Review of Former NFL Reporter Dianna Russini Concludes She Didn't Comply With Standards
articles.summary: An investigation by The Athletic has concluded that former NFL reporter Dianna Russini violated the company's standards because of her relationship with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel that led to her resignation in April.
articles.body:
An investigation by The Athletic has concluded that former NFL reporter Dianna Russini violated the company's standards because of her relationship with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel that led to her resignation in April.

The report drew no conclusions about the nature of Russini's relationship with Vrabel, who said he took accountability for his actions without addressing photos released of the coach and the reporter at a resort in Arizona. He stepped away from the team on the third day of the NFL draft to begin counseling and returned soon afterward.

"We neither completed an investigation nor reached any conclusion about the nature of the full relationship between Vrabel and Russini, but the totality of the public photographs are enough to conclude a violation of company policy," the report said.

Ravens Waiting on NFL's Bateman Investigation

Steven Ginsberg, executive editor at The Athletic, a New York Times-owned sports outlet, addressed the report in a message to employees Thursday.

"We undertook this review to ensure the integrity of our journalism and to maintain the trust our audience places in us. Nothing is more important than our credibility," Ginsberg wrote.

Mike Semel, editorial director for standards and quality at The Athletic, conducted the review of Russini's work, examining 903 stories, 204 episodes of her podcast and 77 videos.

"The review found that the vast majority of Dianna's stories were unrelated to Vrabel, and most of those that mentioned him did not raise concerns," Ginsberg told the staff. "We have, however, added editor's notes to four stories — one written and three videos — that did not meet our standards."

The photos of Vrabel and Russini were taken in Sedona, Arizona, before the annual NFL meetings that began in Phoenix on March 29, according to the New York Post. Vrabel and Russini are both married. The NFL did not investigate Vrabel's actions.

"Russini's relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic's standards," Semel wrote in the report. "Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed."

Vrabel led the Patriots to the Super Bowl in February, where they lost to Seattle. He was the AP NFL Coach of the Year in his first season in New England, finishing 63 points ahead of Jacksonville's Liam Coen.

Russini told the AP on Thursday that she stands by what she wrote in her resignation letter in April.

"I have covered the NFL with professionalism and dedication throughout my career, and I stand behind every story I have ever published. When the Page Six item first appeared, The Athletic supported me unequivocally, expressed confidence in my work and pride in my journalism. For that I am grateful. In the days that followed, unfortunately, commentators in various media have engaged in self-feeding speculation that is simply unmoored from the facts," Russini said then, adding she was stepping away "not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career."

articles.title: Falcons Announce Captains for 2026 NFL Season amid Tua, Michael Penix Jr. QB1 Battle
articles.summary: As the quarterback competition between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. continues, the Atlanta Falcons have chosen not to select a quarterback as one of their captains.
articles.body:
As the quarterback competition between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. continues, the Atlanta Falcons have chosen not to select a quarterback as one of their captains.

The team announced Thursday that this year's captains will be kicker Nick Folk, safety Jessie Bates III, running back Bijan Robinson, guard Chris Lindstrom and linebacker Divine Deablo.

Tagovailoa signed a one-year deal with the Falcons in March after being released by the Dolphins, and he hoped Atlanta could be the place to get his career back on track.

But the former No. 5 overall pick has struggled to establish himself as the team's starter. Even though Penix has spent most of the offseason and training camp rehabbing a torn ACL, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last week that Tagovailoa had lost a "big-time lead" and that "the door is open" for Penix.

Penix, the No. 8 overall pick in 2024, was cleared to practice on Aug. 22.

Tagovailoa is certainly the more proven quarterback of the group, having put together some tremendous seasons in the past and led the Dolphins to the playoffs, but his play last year was a cause for concern.

He threw for 2,660 yards, 20 touchdowns and 15 interceptions in 14 games.

Penix, meanwhile, has still only played in 14 games in his career, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions.

The clock is ticking for the Falcons to make a decision about their quarterback, as they'll open the regular season next Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. With the situation still fluid, the team decided to look to other positions for its captains.

Robinson is the obvious choice given that he's the cornerstone of the franchise. One of the best running backs in the league, Robinson inked a historic deal that ties him to the Falcons through the 2030 campaign.

Robinson, along with new head coach Kevin Stefanski, will look to lead Atlanta to a turnaround season after years of struggle.

articles.title: Michael Wilson Lands Cardinals Contract Extension, Full Details Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals haven't had much to celebrate in recent years, but they created a moment of positivity on Thursday by rewarding one of their rising young stars with a new deal.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals haven't had much to celebrate in recent years, but they created a moment of positivity on Thursday by rewarding one of their rising young stars with a new deal.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Cardinals and wide receiver Michael Wilson agreed to a three-year contract extension worth $75 million that includes $47 million guaranteed.

Wilson enjoyed a breakout season in 2025, recording career highs across the board with 78 catches for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns. He was the first Cardinals receiver to surpass 1,000 yards since DeAndre Hopkins in 2020, and he and tight end Trey McBride (1,239 yards) were the first Cardinals teammates to produce over 1,000 yards in the same season since 2015.

Wilson, McBride and Marvin Harrison Jr. give Arizona a strong crop of young pass-catchers for its future franchise quarterback. The Cardinals used a third-round pick in the 2026 draft to select signal-caller Carson Beck out of Miami, but veteran Jacoby Brissett will open the year as the team's starter against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 13.

Rewarding Wilson is a sign that the Cardinals are moving in the right direction as they try to complete their rebuild and return to playoff contention.

articles.title: Jeff Hafley Reveals Eagles Knew Packers Blitz Packages from Fan Videos Recorded at Training Camp
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley and passing game coordinator Kevin Patullo are on the same side now, but they were on opposing coaching staffs for the 2024 season opener between the Philadelphia Eagles and Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley and passing game coordinator Kevin Patullo are on the same side now, but they were on opposing coaching staffs for the 2024 season opener between the Philadelphia Eagles and Green Bay Packers.

And Patullo's Eagles got the best of Hafley's Packers with a little help from fans video taping Green Bay's training camp.

Hafley, who was Green Bay's defensive coordinator that season, told reporters Thursday that Patullo, who was then Philadelphia's passing game coordinator, revealed to him the Eagles had half of the Packers' blitz packages from fan recordings at training camp that were then posted online.

49ers DE's Hilarious Plan for Australia Flight

"We had a pressure that I had never run, so there's no way he could've known about it," Hafley said. "And they knew it was coming. (Kevin) said they saw that pressure on video."

Notably, Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker was also on Philadelphia's staff that season and also warned about filming at practice during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan (h/t Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News ).

"Once you get past Game 3 or 4, everything is on tape," Parker said. "When you're in Week 1 or 2, you're looking for things. So actually, I don't know if people realize this, I was following some of our media members and stuff even before I got [to the Cowboys] because when I was in Green Bay and Denver and Philadelphia, I've played Dallas in all three spots, us kinda trying to look for things."

Philadelphia's offense had no trouble exploiting the Green Bay defense during the 34-29 victory in that 2024 opener. Saquon Barkley had three touchdowns, A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith combined for 203 receiving yards, and Jalen Hurts finished with 278 yards and two touchdowns through the air.

The Packers managed two sacks, but their defense struggled to get off the field throughout the contest.

It set the tone for the Eagles, who went 14-3 during the regular season before defeating the Packers again in the playoffs on their way to a Super Bowl title. Barkley ran for 2,005 yards as the Offensive Player of the Year, while Hurts finished with 32 total touchdowns with his arm and legs.

And now with some of the assistant coaches from that championship team elsewhere, they are warning against the issues that come with filming during training camp and practice.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Potential Will Levis Landing Spot After Release from Titans Before 2026 Season
articles.summary: The New York Jets worked out free-agent quarterback Will Levis on Thursday following his release from the Tennessee Titans, according to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.
articles.body:
The New York Jets worked out free-agent quarterback Will Levis on Thursday following his release from the Tennessee Titans, according to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.

Rosenblatt added that if the Jets decide to sign Levis, it will be as part of their practice squad.

Levis spent three seasons with the Titans after they selected him in the second round of the 2023 NFL draft, but they cut him on Sunday after deciding to go with Cam Ward and Mitchell Trubisky as the quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.

Levis, 27, did not see any game action last season, but he started 21 contests over the course of 2023 and 2024, posting a 5-16 record.

After throwing for 1,808 yards, eight touchdowns and four interceptions in nine starts as a rookie, Levis was named Tennessee's starter entering 2024, but he did not take a step forward.

Levis went just 2-10 in his 12 starts, completing 63.1 percent of his passes for 2,091 yards, 13 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.

The Titans had the worst record in the NFL in 2024, prompting them to select Ward first overall in the 2025 NFL draft. At that point, the writing was on the wall regarding Levis' future in Tennessee.

Should Levis join the Jets, he will enter into one of the league's most uncertain quarterback situations.

Veteran Geno Smith is New York's starter with rookie fourth-round draft pick Cade Klubnik serving as his backup. The Jets also have Bailey Zappe on their practice squad.

All signs point toward the Jets using a high pick on a quarterback in the 2027 NFL draft, but this season could give one of the existing quarterbacks on their roster to stick around as a backup or bridge starter next season.

Should Levis make it onto the Jets' practice squad and eventually their active roster, it is possible he could establish himself as a long-term option in New York, even if it is in a reserve role.
